item.title: Wave propagation analysis for a second strain gradient rod theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.33083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, an enriched model describing the longitudinal wave propagation is established based on Mindlin's Second Strain Gradient (SSG) theory, which can describe the heterogeneity caused by the micro-structure interactions in the frame of continuum mechanics. The governing equation and associated boundary conditions are derived based on Hamilton's principle, then the dispersion relation of non-classical longitudinal wave together with the extra-waves appearing exclusively in SSG theory model are investigated. The investigations are based on the modal density, energy flow, and forced response of the rod. Wave transmission and reflection through planar interfaces based on the proposed model have been calculated. Finally, the results of the enriched model are well interpreted by comparing with the classical theory results, and some useful conclusions are derived on the SSG theory based model in the wave propagation characterization.
item.dc:creator: Guang Zhu (LTDS), Christophe Droz (LTDS), Abdelmalek Zine (MMCS), Mohamed Ichchou (LTDS)

item.title: Scalar-Longitudinal Modes of Extended Electrodynamics in Perfectly Conducting Cavities and Trapped Modes of Divergence Cleaning
item.description: arXiv:2610.33953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In extended electrodynamics, the Lorenz condition is not imposed and $C=\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}+\mu_0\varepsilon_0\partial\Phi/\partial t$ is a dynamical field, which adds a scalar-longitudinal (SL) family to the TE, TM and TEM modes of a cavity. With $C=0$ on the wall of a closed perfectly conducting cavity, the classical resonances remain unchanged, while the SL modes are the Dirichlet eigenmodes of the volume, with $\mathbf{B}=0$ and an electric field along $\nabla C$. In uniform cavities they share the frequencies of the TM modes that vary along the axis, and for a connected wall the fundamental remains classical. Matching at a conductor described by its constitutive laws gives $\partial C/\partial n=0$ instead and couples the scalar-bearing modes to the Maxwell field. The results belong to the $C=0$ problem, the condition that separates the sectors and the one divergence cleaning imposes. The rectangular, circular cylinder and coaxial cavities provide benchmarks, together with the damping time that gives the slowest scalar mode its fastest decay.
item.dc:creator: Natan Rentzber, Jacob Howard, Fernando Minotti, Anatoliy Pinchuk, Giovanni Modanese

item.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2610.35849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interaction of strong ($a_0>1$), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by $\varepsilon_{\rm B}\equiv a_0\omega_{\rm B}/\omega_0$, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For $\varepsilon_{\rm B}<1$ the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency $\Omega_{\rm B}$ to scattering; when $\Omega_{\rm B}$ exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm p}^{-2/3}$ to $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm B}^{1/2}/\varepsilon_{\rm p}$ wavelengths ($\varepsilon_{\rm p}\equiv a_0\omega_{\rm p}/\omega_0$; $\omega_{\rm p}$ is the plasma frequency). When $a_0^2>\varepsilon_{\rm B}>1$, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.
item.dc:creator: Navin Sridhar (Stanford University)

item.title: Asymptotically accurate and geometric locking-free finite element implementation of a refined shell theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.23369v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate finite element analysis of refined shell theories is crucial but often hindered by membrane and shear locking effects. While various element-based locking-free techniques exist, this work addresses the problem at the theoretical level by utilizing results from asymptotic analysis. A formulation of a 2D refined shell theory incorporating transverse shear is developed using rescaled coordinates and angles of rotation, ensuring equal asymptotic orders of magnitude for extension, bending, and rotation measures and their respective stiffnesses. This novel approach, implemented via isogeometric analysis, is shown to be both asymptotically accurate relative to the underlying refined shell theory and inherently free from membrane and shear locking. Numerical simulations of semi-cylindrical shells show excellent agreement between the analytical solutions, 2D refined shell theory predictions, and 3D elasticity theory, validating the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed formulation.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 446 (2025) 118327
item.dc:creator: Khanh Chau Le, Hoang-Giang Bui

item.title: Deriving the second law of thermodynamics and exploring its boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2607.28765v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The second law of thermodynamics still lacks a general proof applicable to classical and quantum systems across broad ranges of degrees of nonequilibrium, particle interactions, and time scales. In this paper, we show that from Boltzmann's assumption of equal a priori probabilities, the second law naturally emerges via the phase-space continuity equation for the macrostate-level probability $f$ defined over fixed $\Omega$-intervals, where $\Omega$ is the number of microstates. Further analysis suggests a more general assumption underlying the second law: $f$ increases monotonically with $\Omega$, i.e., $\partial f/\partial \Omega > 0$. Based on these findings, the second law can be readily derived for fully chaotic systems. The derivation does not rely on dynamical details, highlighting the statistical nature of entropy increase. For the dilute hard-sphere gas model considered in the H-theorem, the second law may also be established through a simplified approach that requires the Boltzmann equation but does not use the H-function. In contrast, if the positive correlation between $f$ and $\Omega$ breaks down, i.e., $\partial f/\partial \Omega \leq 0$ (e.g., because of local nonchaoticity), the second law of thermodynamics may not apply: entropy can decrease spontaneously with no energetic penalty, and the system can reach an intrinsic-nonequilibrium steady state.
item.dc:creator: Yu Qiao
